blocks.text: Quick verdict

Webshare is the better value for developers and small teams with steady volume: $27.50 for 10 GB against $35 at Decodo, $225 for 100 GB against $275, plus a free datacenter tier for testing. Decodo is the better choice when you need its larger 115M+ pool, pay-as-you-go flexibility for bursty work, mobile proxies, ZIP and ASN targeting together, or scraping APIs. Both reset unused plan traffic monthly, so buy close to real usage either way.

Decodo and Webshare are both self-service favourites with clean dashboards, good APIs and transparent pricing. Webshare is the cheaper of the two at most volumes and adds a permanent free datacenter plan. Decodo has a larger advertised pool, a pay-as-you-go option, mobile proxies and scraping APIs, plus a stronger record in independent benchmarks. This comparison helps you decide whether Decodo's extra quality and breadth are worth paying for.

blocks.text: Decodo in 2026: what you get

Decodo is the 2024 rebrand of Smartproxy, one of the most popular mid-market providers. Its residential network is advertised at 115 million IPs across 195+ locations, and independent benchmarks put its success rate around 99.9% with sub-second response times. Every plan includes the full pool plus city, state, ZIP and ASN targeting, and the dashboard is one of the easiest to set up. Decodo also sells datacenter, ISP and mobile proxies and a family of scraping APIs.

Strengths: Large 115M+ pool at a mid-market price; Near-perfect success rates in independent tests; Clean, fast self-service onboarding; Scraping APIs available when raw proxies are not enough. Weak spots: Plan traffic does not roll over; Published pricing stops at 100 GB; beyond that you need a quote; More expensive per GB than budget brands.
Webshare in 2026: what you get

Webshare is built for developers who want to configure everything themselves. Pricing is transparent, the free datacenter plan makes it easy to test integrations, and paid plans scale smoothly from tiny to large. Its residential network advertises 80M+ IPs across 195 countries. It does not sell mobile proxies or a broad scraping API, and paid plans start with an account-wide limit of 500 concurrent requests.

Strengths: Permanent free datacenter plan for testing; Low, transparent residential pricing; Excellent dashboard and API; Sticky sessions up to 24 hours. Weak spots: Bandwidth resets monthly with no rollover; No mobile proxies; 500-request default concurrency limit.
Pricing: Decodo vs Webshare

Decodo sells residential traffic at $4/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, or on monthly plans: 3 GB for $11.25 ($3.75/GB), 10 GB for $35, 25 GB at $3.25/GB, 50 GB for $150 and 100 GB for $275 ($2.75/GB). Top-ups are billed at your plan's rate, so you are not pushed into the next tier.

Webshare's rotating residential plans cost $3.50 for 1 GB, $27.50 for 10 GB, $65 for 25 GB, $225 for 100 GB and $875 for 500 GB per month, falling to $1.40/GB at 3 TB. Yearly billing is about 30% cheaper but is paid upfront for a 360-day term. Unused bandwidth resets every 30 days.

For a 10 GB month, Webshare costs about $27.50 while Decodo costs about $35, so Webshare saves around 21%. Buying 100 GB, you would pay about $225 with Webshare and $275 with Decodo: a 18% saving in Webshare's favour. Both Decodo and Webshare work on allowances that do not carry forward indefinitely, so size your plan to real monthly usage rather than buying ahead.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Decodo has the bigger advertised network, 115M+ residential IPs against 80M+ for Webshare, roughly 1.4 times larger. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, Decodo lists 195+ countries and Webshare lists 195. On targeting, Decodo offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN, while Webshare offers country, plus state, city or ZIP (US) or ASN.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Decodo offers rotating or sticky sessions with configurable duration, and Webshare offers rotating or sticky from 1 minute to 24 hours. Both use a backconnect gateway: you point your tool at one host and port, and choose country, city or session behaviour through parameters in the username.
Which is better for your use case?
General web scraping: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: a large pool and near-perfect benchmark success rates. How Webshare compares: low prices and a developer-friendly API.
SERP and rank tracking: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: a dedicated SERP scraping API plus city targeting. How Webshare compares: fine for light rank tracking.

Social media and multi-account management: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With Decodo: sticky sessions, sub-users and an easy dashboard. With Webshare: 24-hour sticky sessions and cheap static ISP IPs. Run the same small test on both before committing.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: ZIP targeting and a ready-made e-commerce API. The limitation on the Webshare side: good for US work with ZIP targeting, thinner elsewhere.
Ad verification and geo-testing: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: wide coverage with city and ASN targeting. How Webshare compares: no mobile network and limited selector combinations.
Tight budgets: Webshare. Webshare has the edge here. Why: free tier plus some of the lowest per-GB rates here. How Decodo compares: it is mid-priced, not cheap.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Decodo: Free trial (about 100 MB) on residential. Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial. Verification and payment rules differ too. Decodo: Light KYC; checks on some targets. Webshare: ID checks only when flagged or for restricted categories. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Decodo and Webshare before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Decodo and Webshare is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Decodo: free trial (about 100 MB) on residential; Webshare: 10 free datacenter proxies (1 GB/month); no residential trial).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Decodo comes out ahead in 4, Webshare in 1, and 1 is a tie. That makes Decodo the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Decodo is strongest for small and mid-size scraping teams, while Webshare is strongest for solo developers and small teams. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.

Small and mid-size scraping teams
Developers who want enterprise-like quality without contracts
Mixed workloads that may grow into scraping APIs
Webshare is the better pick for:
Solo developers and small teams
Budget scraping with predictable monthly volume
Buyers who also need cheap datacenter lists
